A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Scalable Equilibrium Sampling with Sequential Boltzmann Generators. All 32 pages, including Appendices A–F, are readable and support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original molecular-sampling experiments in Section 4 and Appendix F, including baseline comparisons, chirality analyses, and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix F, including the quantitative comparisons in Tables 2–3 and 8–10.

M1.justification: The TarFlow proposal, soft equivariance through augmentation, center-of-mass energy adjustment, and AIS/SMC sampling procedure are unchanged, including Algorithms 1–2 and Appendix E.

E1.justification: Both versions use alanine dipeptide, trialanine, alanine tetrapeptide, hexa-alanine, and chignolin. Section 4 and Appendix D retain the same molecular systems and sampling tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: SE(3)-EACF, ECNF, and ECNF++ participate in the same corresponding experiments. The appendix comparisons also retain the same methods and sampling variants.

E3.justification: The data splits, sample counts, metrics, model configurations, and training and sampling settings in Section 4 and Appendices D–F are unchanged. The added direction arrows in Table 3 do not alter the metrics.

E4.justification: Appendix F retains the same chirality analysis, Ramachandran plots, proposal-versus-reweighting comparisons, and ablations of center-of-mass adjustment, weight clipping, sample count, and Langevin timesteps.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 retains the statement that three models are independently trained and sampled wherever ± is reported. Uncertainty displays are unchanged, with no added run counts, seed information, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: The numerical entries and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Figure 8 retains chignolin E-W2 values of 12.046 for SNIS and 3.571 for SMC; Tables 2–3 and 8–10 also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, propositions, assumptions, and derivations are unchanged, including the center-of-mass ESS argument, truncation bounds, and Itô-filtering analysis in Appendices A–C.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and scalability claims: efficient Transformer-based proposals, inference-time annealing, sampling through hexapeptides, and progress on chignolin.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations concerning likelihood estimation, sampling efficiency, mode coverage, and energy-versus-macrostructure tradeoffs. The limitations concerning expensive CNF likelihoods and their use within SBG are unchanged.

D1.justification: The Section 1 code link changes from charliebtan/transferable-samplers to transferable-samplers/transferable-samplers, updating the documented repository destination. Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and timing information are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5, citations throughout the paper, and the bibliography retain the same works and research positioning. No related work or novelty comparison is added or removed.

P1.justification: v3 removes Tong's 'Current: Duke University' affiliation, updates two correspondence addresses, and corrects Kirill Neklyudov's name in the acknowledgements. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds running title headers and downward arrows for the E-W2 and T-W2 columns in Table 3, with minor table-spacing and text-reflow changes. All figures and tables are retained, and the embedded graphics are identical.

improvement.justification: Table 3's direction arrows slightly improve readability, while the remaining edits update presentation, contacts, and the repository address. The scientific argument and all supporting evidence, including appendix analyses, are unchanged. These limited maintenance edits do not establish a meaningful overall quality difference.
